thread.old_title: He is risen, as he said — Psalm 16, the third day of Hosea and Jonah, and the firstfruits sheaf (Leviticus 23; Acts 2; 1 Corinthians 15)
thread.title: He is risen, as he said — Psalm 16, the third day of Hosea and Jonah, and the firstfruits sheaf (Leviticus 23; Acts 2; 1 Corinthians 15)
thread.old_summary:
It ain't new. The women come to the tomb at the end of the Sabbath and are told what he had told them:

*In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1)

*He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6)

*But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.* (Matthew 26:32)

David had written the rising a thousand years before, and Peter and Paul both said this was the verse:

*For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Psalm 16:10)

*He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Messiah (Christ), that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.* (Acts 2:31)

*Wherefore he saith also in another psalm, Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Acts 13:35)

The third day was Hosea's, spoken over the house that would be raised up, and Jonah's, which Yahusha (Jesus) took as his own sign:

*After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.* (Hosea 6:2)

*Now Yahuah (LORD) had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.* (Jonah 1:17)

*For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40)

And the morning itself was in the Torah's calendar. The sheaf of firstfruits is waved before Yahuah (the LORD) on the morrow after the Sabbath, in Passover week, and Paul calls the risen one by the sheaf's name:

*Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest:* (Leviticus 23:10)

*And he shall wave the sheaf before Yahuah (LORD), to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.* (Leviticus 23:11)

*But now is Messiah (Christ) risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.* (1 Corinthians 15:20)

*But every man in his own order: Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ’s) at his coming.* (1 Corinthians 15:23)

A firstfruits sheaf is the first of a harvest, waved so that the rest may be accepted. He rose on the day the sheaf was waved, first of them that slept, and the order Paul gives is the order of the harvest: he first, afterward those that are his at his coming. The rising is also the Father's word over the trial's verdict:

*And declared to be the Son of Elohim (God) with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:* (Romans 1:4)

The council said blasphemy. The empty tomb on the morning of the sheaf said Son of Elohim (God), with power.

cards.src_text: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
cards.tgt_text: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
cards.note: Mark 16:1 — *And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) The same morning from the women's side. The sabbath was past and they had *bought sweet spices* to anoint a body they took to be still in the grave. Matthew gives the hour, Mark gives the errand, and both have the same faithful women walking to the same tomb.
cards.prose: The same morning from the women's side. The sabbath was past and they had *bought sweet spices* to anoint a body they took to be still in the grave. Matthew gives the hour, Mark gives the errand, and both have the same faithful women walking to the same tomb.
cards.member_note: Mark 16:1 — *had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.* The women bought spices once the sabbath was past, so they came expecting a body and not a risen man.

cards.src_text: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
cards.tgt_text: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.
cards.note: Luke 24:1 — *Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) Luke gives the same dawn. They came on the first day, *very early in the morning*, carrying spices they had made ready beforehand. Matthew's women and Luke's are the same faithful witnesses, walking to a tomb they expected to find shut with him inside it.

cards.tgt_text: The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.
cards.note: John 20:1 — *The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) John names Mary Magdalene and says it was *yet dark*. Matthew has the dawn beginning to break. It is one morning seen at two moments, and in both she is among the first to come and the first to see the tomb opened.
